change_summary: First main-process workspace-bar service: entry list, pinned-entry persistence and single-frame switching, with window disappearance tracked through the windows service's destroy event
expected: Smoke test in the running app: after an ordinary close of the presented window, the most-recently-used hidden window is revealed in its place, so exactly one window stays visible.
observed: Closing the presented window left zero visible windows. The remaining windows stayed hidden, their renderers still alive, and the frame vanished from the screen; the service never emitted a reveal.
root_cause: The service tracked window disappearance through the upstream onDidDestroyWindow event, which upstream fires only for windows destroyed after a crash. An ordinary close never reached the service, so nothing triggered the reveal. The test doubles emitted destroy on every close, which is why the unit tests did not see it.
fix_hypothesis: Subscribe per window to onDidClose instead of the windows service's destroy event, and rewrite the test doubles to mirror upstream's real event ordering so the unit suite exercises the same sequence the app produces.
tests_run: smoke test of the running dev build: open three workspaces, close the presented window, count visible windows from the main process
notes: Found only in the running app: the unit suite passed against test doubles whose event ordering did not match upstream's, so the doubles are part of the fix. wall_clock_seconds is recorded as 0 because this trial is logged from the smoke-test finding and no timer was placed around the interactive check; the number is absent, not zero.

change_summary: Reveal driven by each window's onDidClose, with the previous window hidden when the incoming window reports that it has been shown
expected: Smoke test in the running app: never two visible windows at once, including when another window takes over the frame by showing itself rather than through a bar click.
observed: When another window took over via its own show, two windows were visible at the same time for roughly 200 ms before the previous one hid.
root_cause: macOS reports the window show event about 200 ms after the window is actually on screen, so the hide of the outgoing window, which waited for that event, was issued about 200 ms too late.
fix_hypothesis: Make window focus a takeover trigger alongside show, so the outgoing window hides on whichever of the two arrives first.
tests_run: smoke test of the running dev build: force a takeover by showing a second window directly and sample the visible set from the main process
notes: With focus added as a takeover trigger the measured overlap fell from about 200 ms to about 16 ms. wall_clock_seconds is recorded as 0 because this trial is logged from the smoke-test finding and no timer was placed around the interactive check; the number is absent, not zero.
